caption: Members of Castellers de Lleida form a Human Tower in Tarragona, Spain.

Brasília, Brazil Voters wait for a polling station to open in the Cidade Estrutural area of the capital during the first round of a highly polarised presidential election. The election pits the leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, against the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, an ally of Donald Trump and the son of the jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro.

Tigray, Ethiopia A member of the Tigray Peace Force (TPF) inspects an empty police station abandoned by officers as Ethiopian federal and allied forces enter the Tigray capital, Mekelle. There are growing fears of a return to civil war, which claimed 600,000 lives between 2020 and 2022.
Gangwon province, South Korea Tourists ride the Ara Nabi Sea Sky Bicycle in Gangneung. The attraction lets you pedal a bike along a cable out over the sea.
Milan, Italy A demonstrator with a mask depicting the Amazon chief executive, Jeff Bezos, writes the word ‘Stop’ on a wall during a protest march against the construction of new datacentres in Rho.

Manila, Philippines Teddy Arcilla sits with his nine dogs along a pew inside a church before a blessing ceremony to mark World Animal Day, which also coincides with the feast day of Saint Francis of Assisi, the patron saint of animals.

Albacete, Spain Walls marked by floodwater inside a house after flooding in Madrigueras. A 102-year-old woman was found dead in her home and 90 people had to be rescued after torrential rain caused flooding in the region.

Larteh, Ghana A person takes part in a re-enactment of the Katamano war as part of the Odwira festival celebrations. Also known as the battle of Dodowa in many British colonial records, it was fought on 7 August 1826 between the Ashanti empire and coastal states and allied communities with British military assistance.

Machu Picchu, Peru Peruvian firefighters inspect a fire on the Sacred Valley of the Incas, near the main access road to the Unesco world heritage site. One person died and two others suffered burns after fames spread quickly because of the hot, windy weather and dry vegetation, according to the authorities.
credit: IX Cusco Regional Fire Department/AFP/Getty Images

caption: Tarragona, Spain Members of Castellers de Lleida form a human tower during the 30th Concurs de Castells, or Human Tower Competition.
Mannar, Sri Lanka Egrets gather on beach near a windfarm. The Vankalai sanctuary and Mannar island are known for their populations of several egret species.
Málaga, Spain The Caped Crusader takes a bathroom break at San Diego Comic-Con Málaga 2026. Last year’s event was the first international edition of the comic book convention outside the US.

Ohio, US Donald Trump dances during a campaign rally for Republican candidates, including the US senator Jon Husted and the gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, in Vandalia. In his speech, Trump mixed profanity with promises of financial help if the Republicans win the midterms.

West Kalimantan, Indonesia A boy climbs a rope hanging from a barge stranded on a dry riverbed during a severe drought in Sekadau. As of last month, about 80% of Indonesia was under drought conditions, exacerbated by a very strong El Niño event that is expected to peak toward December, according to the country’s meteorology agency.

Sepang, Malaysia Red Bull mechanics change the tyres and inspect the rest of Max Verstappen’s car during a pit stop at the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, held in Malaysia because of the conflict in the Middle East. Verstappen went on to win the race, his first victory of the season.
Staff climb out of windows as flames engulf the National Academy of Sciences.

Tel Aviv, Israel Passengers, who experienced an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia after an attempted attack on a flydubai plane, arrive at Ben Gurion airport. Capt Smit Machchhar, the Indian pilot who helped thwart the apparent attempt to crash a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv, said his faith and his desire to save his passengers allowed him to make a ‘last push’ to open the cockpit door as he fought for his life.

Jabaliya, Gaza Palestinian children play football in a refugee camp amid the ruins of buildings destroyed by Israeli airstrikes. More than 2.1 million displaced people are living in tents and temporary shelters in Gaza, where about 82% of structures – roughly 200,000 buildings – have been damaged, with about two-thirds of those destroyed, according to the UN agency for Palestinian refugees, Unrwa.

Jenin, West Bank Children play on heavy machinery parked along the roadside as Israelis march between the settlements of Ganim and Kadim on the outskirts of the occupied West Bank city of Jenin. More than 60 Palestinian communities in the occupied West Bank have been wiped off the map since October 2023 and 18 others have been partly displaced, according to the Israeli rights group B’Tselem. Nearly 5,000 people have been forced from their homes, almost half of them children.

Mansouri, Lebanon The town of Mansouri, which sits in the Israeli-occupied buffer zone of southern Lebanon , is bombarded as the Israeli military said it was carrying out an operation to destroy alleged Hezbollah infrastructure such as tunnels.

Paris, France A police officer stands next to the burned entrance of Roger Verlomme secondary school following a blockade by protesting students in Paris. The French government is struggling to deal with its worst crisis in months after it was taken by surprise by the thousands of teenagers demonstrating outside schools across the country this week.

Paris, France French gendarmes run amid clashes with high-school students near the Lycée Berthelot high school in Aubervilliers. Many school students protesting have accused the state of disengaging from secondary education , describing difficult conditions in classrooms with ceilings partially collapsing during class, leaks, cockroaches and buildings in disrepair.

Kyiv, Ukraine Emergency workers carry away a casualty from a building of the National Academy of Sciences hit by a Russian jet-powered drone. Anatoliy Zagorodny, the president of the national academy, said the blast struck while many staff members were inside . He said he did not know why Russia had targeted a leading centre of scientific research. ‘We are not connected with the military. This is an attack on science. It is terrorism,’ he said.

Kharkiv, Ukraine A rescue dog searches a multistorey residential building hit by a Russian airstrike. Russia has signalled that its attacks on Ukraine could intensify , and US-brokered efforts to end the war show little sign of progress.

Sofiivska Borshchahivka, Ukraine One man comforts another near the body of an acquaintance killed in a Russian drone strike on a wholesale food market. Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, called on western countries to intensify their pressure on Russia . ‘Every Russian terrorist attack is a loss of life that could have been prevented if pressure on Russia had finally become total,’ he wrote on X this week. ‘The world must understand that terrorists will go further if they are not stopped here, in Ukraine. And we cannot turn a blind eye to such brutal strikes’.
Bangkok, Thailand Residents wade through flood water on Phetchaburi Road. The city was hit by 300mm (12in) of rain at the weekend and all 50 of its districts were declared disaster zones.
Bangkok, Thailand People carry water bottles through flood waters in Bangkok.

Puerto San Carlos, Mexico A man crosses a flooded street after Hurricane Polo , the second-most intense Pacific hurricane on record. It brought high winds and heavy rains and resulted in seven deaths.

Tehran, Iran Missiles, air defence systems and unmanned aerial vehicles are displayed at Baharestan Square for Iran’s ‘sacred defence week’. The US military is dispatching a third aircraft carrier strike group to the Middle East, as Donald Trump warned new strikes against Iran could be on the horizon.
Delhi, India Exiled Tibetans shout slogans from a police vehicle after being detained during a protest outside the Chinese embassy on China’s National Day.

Gravelines, France A police officer patrols the beach at Petit-Fort-Philippe looking for migrants trying to cross the Channel. A Paris court this week jailed six ⁠men for manslaughter over the deaths of at least 27 people in the worst mass drowning on record from a small-boat crossing in the Channel.

Portadown, Northern Ireland People gather at Garvaghy Road, a Catholic enclave in the largely Protestant town of Portadown, on the day members of the Orange Order were expected to march through the area for the Drumcree parade. Talks aimed at resolving the Drumcree parade dispute have broken up without agreement, with the Northern Ireland secretary, Chris Bryant, describing the situation as being between a ‘rock and a hard place’.

Texas, US A SpaceX Starship takes off from its launch pad at Boca Chica Beach. SpaceX sent its enormous Starship rocket into Earth’s orbit for the first time on a milestone flight intended to pave the way for future missions to the moon and Mars.
Sicily, Italy Visitors climb Mount Etna as smoke rises from its volcanic cone near Catania. Its eruption on Saturday sent ash plumes 14,000ft into the sky.

Galápagos, Ecuador A whale shark swims near Roca Redonda, a small islet north of Isabela Island in the Galápagos archipelago. It was spotted on a field expedition mounted by the Charles Darwin Foundation.
Police officers detain a struggling protester amid a dense crowd during a demonstration.
London, UK A stag in the mist during the annual rutting season in Richmond Park. The national nature reserve is home to more than 630 red and fallow deer.
Llanrwst, UK A Virginia creeper ( Parthenocissus quinquefolia ) is a blaze of autumnal colours at the Tu Hwnt l’r Bont tea rooms.

Lyon, France Young people hold a sign that says ‘stop budget cuts ’ during a nationwide protest by high-school students over long hours, teacher shortages and decaying facilities. Dozens of schools have been damaged and nearly 3,000 teenagers have been detained since the start of the tensions.

Strasbourg, France Students kick back teargas canisters as they carry out a blockade of the city’s university. French media reports say more than 560 schools and educational establishments have been disrupted by the unrest.

Les Brenets, Switzerland A giant ‘Help’ is written on the grass-covered bed of what was Lac des Brenets, part of the Doubs River. The river dried up in July because of a combination of factors, including geological fissures that drain water underground, below-average rainfall and repeated heatwaves.

San Blas, Mexico Waves crash along Los Cocos beach as Hurricane Rachel strengthens into a category 3 system off the country’s Pacific coast. Northern Mexico is still recovering from Hurricane Polo, with the unusually active Pacific hurricane season being attributed to El Niño.
Shexiang, China An aerial view of the land fingerprint concert held during the National Day celebrations at the ancient town in south-west Guizhou province.
Santiago, Chile A water cannon is fired towards students protesting against budget cuts to the education and welfare system proposed by José Antonio Kast, the country’s new far-right president.

Madrid, Spain Protesters gather outside the Spanish parliament calling for housing reform after the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal, who was forcibly removed from the apartment where she had lived for the last 71 years.

Seoul, South Korea Tom Cruise meets fans on the red carpet at the premiere of his movie Digger. The film by the Oscar-winning Mexican director Alejandro González Iñárritu has received mixed reviews, with some critics describing it as a ‘love it or hate it’ movie.

Ceuta, Spain A young man dives into the strait of Gibraltar. Thousands of people, most of them young Moroccan men, have been living in makeshift settlements in the autonomous city on the north African coast since a mass arrival at the end of July.

Lelystad, Netherlands A replica of the Batavia, an early 17th-century Dutch merchant ship, is transported to its new home on the grounds of Museum Batavialand. The original vessel was shipwrecked off what eventually became known as Western Australia in 1629.

Wehrheim, Germany A commuter train cuts through the morning mist towards Frankfurt. Germany plans to spend €100bn through to 2030 on modernising the rail operator Deutsche Bahn’s dilapidated infrastructure after decades of underinvestment.

Sepang, Malaysia Racing Bulls driver Arvid Lindblad in action during the free practice session for the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix. The race is being held in Malaysia because of the conflict in the Middle East.

Durant, US Donald Trump addresses a midterm election rally for the Republican gubernatorial candidate Mike Mazzei at the Choctaw Event Center in Oklahoma. Trump’s appearance was part of a 32-day campaign blitz amid his record low approval ratings.
Mexico City, Mexico Santa Muerte devotees visit the altar on Alfarería Street in the Tepito neighbourhood of the Mexican capital to pay homage to the Niña Blanca deity.

Naucalpan, Mexico Members of the country’s national guard help its smallest recruit, Comando, to prepare for a training session. The 13-month-old chihuahua is being trained for search-and-rescue missions and to help build a friendlier image of the security force.
New York, US People arrive at the annual Diner en Blanc, a large-scale picnic that brings together foodies, culture enthusiasts and fashionistas. This year’s theme was Parisian belle époque.

New Delhi, India Police officers detain a woman during a protest demanding the resignation of the country’s chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar. The demonstration was called by the gen Z-led Cockroach movement, which in July forced the education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign after weeks of protests calling for education reforms.
Jabal al-Armas, West Bank Israeli military personnel fire teargas as illegal settlers attack Palestinian farmers during the first day of the olive harvest.
Whitley Bay, UK The sun rises at St Mary’s lighthouse on the north-east coast. Built in the late 19th century, the now-listed lighthouse remained operational until the mid-1980s.
